mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring threshold conditions.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 20-day returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or correlation with returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that increases consumer spending and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 3.5%, 5-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) and interest rates (FEDFUNDS) signals dovish monetary policy that reduces real rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Interaction effect between CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS is not significant (p > 0.05), or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO < 100) indicates reduced industrial output and lower corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days during supply contraction regimes.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC for INDPRO is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) reflect strong consumer confidence and economic activity, directly translating to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for HOUST predicting 20-day returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or correlation is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) triggers monetary policy tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Interaction between PAYEMS and UNRATE is not significant (p > 0.05), or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 2.0%, 60-day forward returns are negative in >60% of cases, or Rank IC is below 0.03.
